doc.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Delta humor and Nat King Cole as his early model
summary: Delta speech was exaggeration and understatement; the King Cole Trio influenced him more than the blues then.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: So I’d like to hold that in reserve for a bit. Here’s a quote that you said to someone, I don’t recall who. You said, “In the Mississippi Delta, nobody says anything straight out.”
“Everything is exaggerated or understated, and there’s a lot of humorous sayings and all that, so I was introduced to all that early.”
That’s a quality of your lyrics and songs.
After you wrote “The 14-Day Palmolive Plan,” did you start writing more songs?
No, I don’t think so. I wrote a few songs. I was listening to Nat King Cole at that time, and I... I don’t know.
While you were in high school you were listening to Nat King Cole, when he had the trio and...
So that was a sound and approach that you... It wasn’t a particularly blues-influenced style.
Well, he sang the blues, and... I started listening to the King Cole Trio early, and I was influenced by them a lot moreso than the blues. I went back to the blues later.
